findings.reason: a worker cannot satisfy all four assertions with the fixture as described, and whichever half it abandons (the conflict-merge coverage or the False classification) silently drops the guard the other round of reviews added.
findings.text: §3's fixture holds "a run-owned merge whose conflict resolution edits a runtime source path", and the done-when then requires `changes_runtime_source` to be False "for a delta of a test and an evidence fragment" while the fourth assertion requires the same runtime path to stay in the delta and to make `changes_runtime_source` True; one fixture yields one delta, so the two assertions cannot both hold, and the negative control "restoring the two-dot call fails the test ... on the runtime classification" also cannot fail when the correct delta is already classified True

findings.reason: implementing §3 as written makes the lander and the reflex disagree about a figure review being owed, so the lander would promote past an unanswered figure review, and the repair for that lives in a file the node is not permitted to touch.
findings.text: §3 changes `_changed_figure_paths` to return `None` for an uncomparable history and to have the reflex "compose a full figure review rather than an empty one", but `_owed_review_tiers` (`reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:141-156`) consumes the same helper and its docstring states the opposite reading — "a changed-path list git cannot produce reads as no figure review owed, which is the reflex's own reading of it ... the two must answer alike" — and `reckon/crew/queue_landing.py` is not among the three declared write paths

response_events.note: the test now uses two fixtures: a test-and-fragment delta asserting changes_runtime_source False, and a conflicted run-owned merge editing runtime source asserting the path stays in the delta and the classification is True; each negative control names its fixture
